mainTopic: The amounts and parts of the grape forbidden to a נזיר, and the dispute between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן over leaves and tendrils
overview: The משנה first brings an older ruling: a נזיר is liable only for drinking a רביעית of wine. רבי עקיבא says a כזית is enough, even of bread soaked in wine. He adds that wine, grapes, חרצנים and זגים each carry a separate liability. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה requires two חרצנים and one זג, and רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue over which part of the grape each word means. The גמרא shows that the משנה limits the prohibition to the fruit of the vine, unlike רבי אלעזר, who forbids even leaves and tendrils. It explains that רבי אלעזר reads the פסוקים with ריבויי ומיעוטי, which forbids everything except the branches. The רבנן read them with כללי ופרטי: detail, general phrase, detail, so only fruit and fruit waste are forbidden. The גמרא then explains what that adds (unripe grapes, wormy grapes, and the part between seeds and skin) and why the second detail 'from pits to skin' is needed. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier version: liable only for a quarter-log of wine
steps.stepSummary: An older version of the משנה said a נזיר is liable only once he drinks a רביעית of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first version of the משנה says: he is not liable until he drinks a quarter-log of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings an older, earlier version of the law. It says a נזיר gets lashes only for drinking a full רביעית of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a fairly large amount, a רביעית, as the minimum that makes a נזיר liable for wine. It also sets up רבי עקיבא's view in the next step, which uses a smaller amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The first or earlier version of the משנה
A quarter of a לוג, a liquid measure
Liable to punishment (here, lashes)

steps.confusionAlert: משנה ראשונה here does not mean 'the first משנה of the chapter.' It means an older version of this law, which was later replaced.

phrases.english: The first version of the mishna says:
Not until he drinks a quarter-log of wine.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the earlier version, a נזיר is liable only once he drinks a רביעית of wine.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: an olive-bulk of bread and wine together is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says that bread soaked in wine, if together they make a כזית, makes the נזיר liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: even if he soaked his bread in wine, and together there is enough to make an olive-bulk, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with the older version. He says the amount is a כזית, and the wine can even join together with bread to reach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things change here. First, the amount drops from a רביעית to a כזית. Second, the wine does not have to be eaten alone: the bread soaked in it can count toward the כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Soaked
To combine, to join together toward the required amount
An olive-bulk, a standard amount for eating

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that something permitted can join with something forbidden to make up the amount, is what the גמרא later discusses at length.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Even if he soaked his bread in wine
and there is enough in it to combine
to an olive-bulk, he is liable,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ שָׁרָה פִּיתּוֹ בְּיַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the earlier version's requirement of a רביעית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כזית of wine combined with bread makes a נזיר liable.

steps.title: A separate liability for each kind of grape product
steps.stepSummary: The נזיר is liable separately for wine, grapes, חרצנים and זגים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is liable for wine by itself, for grapes by themselves, for חרצנים by themselves, and for זגים by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists four grape products. Each one is its own separate prohibition for a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is counted on its own, so eating several of them can bring several sets of lashes. Each one is not just one part of a single general ban on grapes.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself, separately
Grapes
One part of the grape (which part is debated below)
Another part of the grape (which part is debated below)

phrases.english: And he is liable for wine by itself,
and for grapes by themselves,
and for ḥartzannim by themselves,
and for zaggim by themselves.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine, grapes, חרצנים and זגים are each a separate prohibition.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: two חרצנים and one זג
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says he is liable only if he eats two חרצנים and one זג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: he is not liable until he eats two חרצנים and a זג.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה gives a different minimum for these grape parts. He requires two חרצנים together with one זג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the exact wording of the פסוק: חרצנים is plural, so at least two, and זג is singular, so one. Only eating that combination makes him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Singular of זגים
Two

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
He is not liable until he eats
two ḥartzannim and a zag.
phrases.notes: Based on the פסוק 'מחרצנים ועד זג', במדבר 6:4.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability requires two חרצנים and one זג.

steps.title: What exactly are חרצנים and זגים?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks which part of the grape each word refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which are the חרצנים, and which are the זגים?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה stops to define its terms. This question sets up the answers in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has used חרצנים and זגים as separate prohibitions, so it now needs to say which part of the grape is which.

keyTerms.meaning: Which are these, what are they

phrases.english: Which are ḥartzannim
and which are zaggim?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ הֵן חַרְצַנִּים וְאֵלּוּ הֵן זַגִּים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the grape is called חרצנים and which is called זגים

steps.title: רבי יהודה: חרצנים are outside, זגים are inside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says חרצנים are the outer parts (the skin) and זגים are the inner parts (the seeds).
steps.simpleTranslation: The חרצנים are the outer parts, and the זגים are the inner parts. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the question. In his view, חרצנים means the outside of the grape and זגים means the inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in his view, חרצנים are the skins and זגים are the seeds. רבי יוסי will argue with this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer parts
The inner parts

phrases.english: The ḥartzannim are the outer ones,
the zaggim are the inner ones,
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of definitions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חרצנים are the outer parts and זגים are the inner parts.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the opposite, remembered by an animal's bell
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the reverse: the outside is the זג, like the outer shell of a bell, and the inside is like the clapper.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: so that you do not make a mistake, think of an animal's bell. The outer part is called the זוג, and the inner part is called the עינבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי יהודה and gives a memory aid. A bell's outer shell is called a זוג, so the outer skin of the grape is the זג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the outside of the bell is the זוג, the grape's skin is the זג, and the seeds inside must be the חרצנים. This is the exact opposite of רבי יהודה's definition.

keyTerms.meaning: So that you do not make a mistake
A bell, specifically its outer shell
The clapper inside a bell
Animal

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: חרצנים = outside, זגים = inside. רבי יוסי: the reverse, זג = outside, like the shell of a bell.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says, so that you do not err:
Like an animal's bell;
phrases.notes: The word זוג (bell) sounds like זג, and that is the hint.

phrases.english: the outer part is the zog,
and the inner part is the inbal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's definition
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זג is the outer skin of the grape, like the outer shell of a bell; the inner part, the seeds, are the חרצנים.

steps.title: Only what grows out of the vine is forbidden, not the vine itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה and infers that only the produce of the vine is forbidden to a נזיר, not the plant itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said three things are forbidden to a נזיר: impurity, and so on. It speaks of what comes out of the vine. So what comes out of the vine is forbidden, but the vine itself is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting the משנה and reading its wording closely. It is setting up the next move, which is to ask whose opinion this matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids 'what comes out of the vine.' The גמרא reads this precisely: the fruit and its products are included, but the plant itself (wood, leaves) is not. This exact reading will clash with another opinion in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
What comes out of the vine: its fruit and products
The vine plant itself
Yes / no: the way the גמרא marks what a phrase includes and what it leaves out

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Three types of things are forbidden to a nazir:
impurity, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the rest of the line: shaving, and everything that comes out of the vine.

phrases.english: What comes out of the vine: yes, it is forbidden.
The vine itself: no, it is not forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַגֶּפֶן — אִין. גֶּפֶן עַצְמוֹ — לָא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by reading the משנה's first line closely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the משנה's wording, only the produce of the vine is forbidden to a נזיר, not the vine itself.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this משנה disagrees with רבי אלעזר, who says in a ברייתא that even leaves and tendrils are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: So our משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר. A ברייתא teaches that רבי אלעזר says even the leaves and tendrils are included in the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names whose opinion the משנה does not follow and brings a ברייתא to show that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says the leaves and young shoots of the vine are also forbidden to a נזיר. Since our משנה limits the prohibition to what comes out of the vine, it cannot match his view. So the משנה follows the other opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Leaves
Tendrils or young shoots of the vine
Included in what the prohibition covers

steps.whatToRemember: By the first version, the משנה's words 'what comes out of the vine' leave out the vine plant itself, so the משנה is not like רבי אלעזר, who forbids even leaves and tendrils.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in line with Rabbi Elazar.
As it was taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
Even leaves and tendrils are included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 8 to show the משנה is not like רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אלעזר includes leaves and tendrils.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר's broader view of the vine prohibition.

steps.title: A second version: the inference comes from the later line about eating grapes
steps.stepSummary: Some say the inference was made from a later line of the משנה: a נזיר is liable only once he eats a כזית of grapes. So grapes count, but the vine itself does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this comment was made on the later part of the משנה: he is liable only once he eats a כזית of grapes. From grapes, yes. From the vine itself, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of where the same inference comes from. It is setting up the same conclusion again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the opening line, this version reads the סיפא, which speaks of eating a כזית 'of grapes.' Mentioning grapes suggests the vine plant itself does not make him liable. The source changes, but the result stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
An olive-sized amount, the minimum that makes him liable
Grapes
Liable, here to lashes

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same point, just drawn from a different line of the משנה.

phrases.english: Some say it was said on the later part:
He is not liable unless
he eats an olive-sized amount of the grapes.
From the grapes: yes, he is liable,
from the vine itself: no, he is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the inference of step 8 from the משנה's first line to its later line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability needs a כזית of grapes, which suggests eating the vine plant itself does not make him liable.

steps.title: In this version too, the משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The second version reaches the same result: the משנה is not like רבי אלעזר, who includes leaves and tendrils.
steps.simpleTranslation: So our משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר. A ברייתא teaches that רבי אלעזר says even the leaves and tendrils are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same conclusion and source for the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the סיפא makes liability depend on grapes, the משנה does not hold like רבי אלעזר, who forbids the leaves and tendrils too. Both versions agree on the result and differ only on which line of the משנה it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Not like: shows whose opinion the משנה does not follow
Even

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree: our משנה limits the נזיר's vine prohibition to the fruit, unlike רבי אלעזר. They differ only on whether this is read from the רישא or the סיפא.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in line with Rabbi Elazar,
as it was taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
Even leaves and tendrils are included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the second version with the same conclusion as step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same ברייתא of רבי אלעזר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In either version, the משנה limits the prohibition to the vine's produce and does not follow רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lies at the root of the argument between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן about leaves and tendrils.
steps.simpleTranslation: With regard to what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next move: why do רבי אלעזר and the רבנן disagree? It wants the underlying reason, not just the two rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9 and 11 showed that the משנה forbids only the produce of the vine, while רבי אלעזר forbids even leaves and tendrils. Now the גמרא looks for the source-based reason behind each side.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to what do they disagree? (asks for the root of a dispute)

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי אלעזר and the רבנן whose view our משנה follows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having shown that the משנה disagrees with רבי אלעזר, the גמרא now asks for the root of that disagreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying basis for the dispute between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן about whether leaves and tendrils are forbidden to a נזיר.

steps.title: Two different methods of reading the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוקים using ריבויי ומיעוטי, and the רבנן use כללי ופרטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר interprets using 'broadenings and limitings,' and the רבנן interpret using 'generalities and specifics.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sides read the same פסוקים with different rules of interpretation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ריבויי ומיעוטי, a broadening phrase usually wins and includes almost everything. With כללי ופרטי, the general phrase is shaped by the specific item, so only things similar to it are included. Each method produces a different list of what a נזיר may not eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Broadenings and limitings: a method where an inclusive phrase can widen the law
Generalities and specifics: a method where a general phrase is defined by a specific example
Interprets, derives law from the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides learn from the same פסוקים. They argue about how to read them, not about which פסוק applies.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar interprets with broadenings and limitings,
the Rabbis interpret with generalities and specifics.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דָּרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי, רַבָּנַן דָּרְשִׁי כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute comes from two different methods of interpretation: ריבויי ומיעוטי for רבי אלעזר and כללי ופרטי for the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties a practical question about a נזיר to a basic disagreement over how the Torah's wording is read.

steps.title: How רבי אלעזר reads the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: "From wine and strong drink he shall abstain" limits, and "anything made from the grapevine" broadens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר interprets with broadenings and limitings. "From wine and strong drink he shall abstain" limits. "Anything that is made from the grapevine" broadens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows רבי אלעזר's method on the actual פסוקים. It points out which phrase limits and which phrase broadens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first phrase names only wine and strong drink, so it narrows the איסור. The next phrase, "anything made from the grapevine," widens it. The order matters: a limiting phrase comes first, and a broadening phrase follows.

keyTerms.meaning: It limited (the phrase narrows the law)
It broadened (the phrase widens the law)
He shall abstain (the root of the word נזיר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar interprets with broadenings and limitings:
"From wine and strong drink he shall abstain" — it limited,
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:3

phrases.english: "From anything that is made from the grapevine" — it broadened.
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 13's mention of רבי אלעזר's method by applying it to the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי אלעזר's reading, the נזיר פסוקים form a limiting phrase (wine and strong drink) followed by a broadening phrase (anything from the vine).

steps.title: A limit followed by a broadening includes everything
steps.stepSummary: Under the rules of ריבויי ומיעוטי, when a limit is followed by a broadening, almost everything is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It limited and then broadened, so it broadened to include everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the general rule of רבי אלעזר's method: a limiting phrase followed by a broadening phrase includes nearly everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule is why רבי אלעזר arrives at such a wide איסור. The broadening phrase is stronger than the limiting phrase, so leaves and tendrils are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: It broadened to include everything

phrases.english: It limited and broadened — it broadened to include everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the limit and broadening identified in step 14 and applies the rule for how such a pair works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a limiting phrase is followed by a broadening phrase, the result includes almost everything.

steps.title: Everything from the vine is included except the branches
steps.stepSummary: The broadening includes everything from the vine. The limiting phrase still excludes one thing: the branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did it broaden? It broadened all things. What did it limit? It limited the branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the result of רבי אלעזר's reading. Everything that comes from the vine is forbidden except the branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the broadening wins, the limiting phrase cannot be meaningless, so it must exclude something. That one exclusion is the branches. Leaves and tendrils are therefore forbidden, which matches רבי אלעזר's ruling in steps 9 and 11.

keyTerms.meaning: All things
Branches (the vine's woody shoots)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אלעזר: limit, then broaden, equals almost everything. So all parts of the vine are forbidden to a נזיר except the branches.

phrases.english: What did it broaden? It broadened all things.
phrases.notes: He means all things that come from the vine, including leaves and tendrils.

phrases.english: What did it limit? It limited the branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out exactly what the 'everything' of step 15 includes and what the limiting phrase still excludes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי אלעזר, a נזיר may not eat anything from the vine, including leaves and tendrils. Only the branches are excluded.

steps.title: The רבנן read the verses as detail, general phrase, detail
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use כללי ופרטי. 'Wine and strong drink' is a detail, 'anything made from the grapevine' is a general phrase, and 'from seeds to skin' is a second detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן explain the פסוקים using the rule of general phrases and details. 'He shall abstain from wine and strong drink' is a detail. 'Anything made from the grapevine' is a general phrase. 'From seeds to skin' goes back and gives a detail again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the רבנן's side, the second half of the answer from Step 13. It breaks the פסוקים into three parts: detail, general phrase, detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same words רבי אלעזר read as 'limit' and 'broadening.' The רבנן read them as details and a general phrase, and they also count the last phrase, 'from seeds to skin,' as a second detail. This three-part pattern is what changes the result.

keyTerms.meaning: A way of reading פסוקים that looks at general phrases and specific details
A detail, meaning a specific item the פסוק names
A general phrase that covers a wide group
It went back and gave a detail again
Two parts of the grape, the seeds and the skin

phrases.english: And the Rabbis interpret using general phrases and details:
"He shall abstain from wine and strong drink": it gave a detail,
phrases.notes: במדבר ו:ג

phrases.english: "Anything made from the grapevine": it gave a general phrase,
phrases.notes: במדבר ו:ד

phrases.english: "From seeds to skin": it went back and gave a detail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the same פסוקים, side by side with רבי אלעזר's reading in Steps 14-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוקים form a pattern of detail, general phrase, detail.

steps.title: Only fruit and fruit waste are included
steps.stepSummary: With detail, general phrase, detail, you include only things like the details. The details are fruit and fruit waste, so only fruit and fruit waste are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When there is a detail, then a general phrase, then a detail, you only include things similar to the detail. The details clearly name fruit and fruit waste, so everything included must be fruit or fruit waste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the rule to reach the רבנן's result. Only things like the details are forbidden, so leaves and tendrils are not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general phrase does add items, but only items similar to the details. Seeds and skin are fruit waste and wine is from the fruit, so the common feature is 'fruit or fruit waste.' Leaves and tendrils are neither, so they stay permitted. That is the רבנן's side of the argument from Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to the detail
Clearly stated
Fruit waste, the leftover parts of the fruit like seeds and skin
